title: AArch64 tiled matmul schedule-unroll: LLVM evidence, Raspberry Pi calibration, and opt-in compiler-side selection

pipeline.compilation: hir.fused_matmul_bias_relu (HIR) -> hir-matmul-bias-relu-to-linalg -> project-owned Transform-dialect script (tile+fuse+K-unroll+vectorize, stock Transform-dialect combinators only) -> stock MLIR-to-LLVM-dialect lowering -> mlir-translate -> LLVM IR -> llc (unmodified LLVM 21.1.8 instruction selection, machine scheduler, greedy register allocator) -> AArch64 object
pipeline.opt_in_selector: tools/select_and_compile_aarch64_matmul_schedule.py (Stage 15) -- sits ABOVE the compile script, never replaces or duplicates its materialization mechanism

transformation.name: K-loop unroll (Option A from the Stage 8/9 design gate)
transformation.mechanism: stock transform.loop.unroll applied to the K-reduction scf.for loop, factor = schedule-unroll-k, immediately after K-tiling and before vectorization
transformation.what_llvm_owns: instruction selection, the pre-RA machine scheduler, register allocation (greedy), spill/reload insertion, prologue/epilogue generation -- entirely unmodified LLVM 21.1.8
transformation.what_this_project_owns: the choice of WHERE to apply a stock Transform-dialect op and, as of Stage 15, an opt-in Python driver that ranks/selects the unroll factor before invoking the unmodified compile pipeline

supported_tiles_note: Stage 11 structurally validated only these three tile configurations. No larger tile (in any dimension) has ever been structurally validated -- Stage 17 explicitly documented this as an untested dimension, not an oversight.
unroll_factor_note: factor must evenly divide the K-loop's pre-unroll trip count (shape_k / tile_k); factor=1 is a verified byte-identical no-op; factor equal to the trip count fully collapses the K-loop (verified structurally, not merely assumed).
measured_domains_note: 6 of 6 tested domains measured schedule-unroll-k=4 as the fastest candidate, each independently, on real Raspberry Pi 5 Cortex-A76 hardware. No counterexample (a domain where uk1 or uk2 wins) was found despite Stage 17 deliberately searching for one using domains chosen to stress uk4's known costs (spilling, small-problem fixed overhead, high K-trip-count live ranges). This is reported as-is and does NOT establish universal optimality -- see truth_boundary below.

correctness.tolerance_policy: max_abs_error < 1e-3 (repository-established threshold, unchanged throughout); every measured candidate was in fact bit-exact (max_abs_error = 0), not merely within tolerance

backend_evidence.source: unmodified LLVM 21.1.8 MIR at 5 pass boundaries (finalize-isel, machine-scheduler before/after, virtregrewriter, prologepilog), extracted and analyzed by project-owned Python tooling (tools/extract_aarch64_candidate_mir.py, tools/analyze_aarch64_candidate_mir.py, tools/analyze_aarch64_machine_schedule.py)
backend_evidence.static_model_top_choice_agreement: 2 of 6 domains (33%) -- exactly the 2 domains where the measured winner happens to be spill-free (cube64, highK)
backend_evidence.static_model_conclusion: No currently collected static metric reliably predicts the measured winner across the tested domain set; static evidence remains useful for cost/risk characterization (it never hid a single real spill) but is not a reliable standalone winner predictor.

calibrated_evidence.mechanism: opt-in --schedule-candidate-mode=calibrated, requires an explicit --schedule-profile; ranks using RANKING_MODE_CALIBRATED_PI (tools/aarch64_schedule_candidate_model.py), falls back deterministically (exact match -> cross-shape bucket -> static -> conservative uk1) when compatible evidence is absent
calibrated_evidence.exact_domain_selection_accuracy: 6 of 6 domains: calibrated mode selected the real measured winner in every domain with compatible evidence
calibrated_evidence.cross_domain_rejection_note: every one of 30 cross-domain compatibility checks across the 6 domains (6 domains x 5 others) correctly rejected exact-match reuse; same-tile domains get a reduced-confidence cross-shape bucket (confidence 0.7), never an exact match; different-tile domains are fully incompatible

truth_boundary.supported_claim: For the tested Raspberry Pi 5 Cortex-A76 path, FP32, the tiled AArch64 matmul-bias-relu NEON microkernel, schedule-unroll-k=4 was the measured fastest candidate in all 6 independently tested shape/tile domains.
NOT_claimed: universal uk4 optimality across untested shapes, tiles, targets, or kernel families
a custom LLVM scheduler or scheduling pass
arbitrary loop scheduling or software pipelining
default/automatic calibrated-mode or uk4 selection anywhere in the compiler
truth_boundary.default_compiler_behavior: unchanged -- --schedule-candidate-mode defaults to manual everywhere; calibrated mode and any uk4 preference are opt-in only, in every driver invocation across Stages 15-17

limitations: No tile larger than 8x8x8 in any dimension has ever been structurally validated (Stage 11 scope).
No target other than Raspberry Pi 5 Cortex-A76 has ever been measured.
No dtype other than f32 has ever been measured.
No kernel family other than the tiled fused matmul-bias-relu microkernel has ever been measured.

perf/hardware performance counters are unavailable on this Pi; no instruction-cache-miss or cycle-level counter evidence exists anywhere in this evidence chain -- code size and llvm-mca estimates are used as labeled static signals only.
Only 6 domains, each backed by a single measurement session (5 interleaved groups); no domain has been independently reproduced across separate days/reboots.

The register-pressure heuristic (approx_peak_live_vector_registers) is a linear scan with no loop-back-edge modeling, not a dataflow analysis -- documented and never used as a scoring signal by default.

Selection happens in a Python compiler driver, not a native C++ MLIR pass -- accurately described throughout as 'opt-in compiler-driver schedule candidate selection controlling a real MLIR schedule materialization pass.'
